column1: # Reference surfaces this port does not carry, and the reason for each.
# "renderer" names a library or format one of the reference's two markdown renderers draws with.
# "component" names a piece of one of its own UI surfaces: a row kind, a node type, a field a card reads.
# "prompt" names a harness system-message section rather than a callable surface.
# Historical rows measured against CLI 2.1.257 and desktop app 1.44121.2.0.
# Implemented 01-15 rows refreshed against CLI 2.1.260 / Desktop 1.46388.3.0 on 2026-09-08.
# Native engine/transport adaptations and private account dependencies remain explicit.
# This file is the other half of ported-text-deltas.tsv. That one asks "is the
# text we send still the reference's text"; this one asks "is the surface we
# offer still the reference's surface" — a question no test could answer while
# the only record of it was prose in CLAUDE.md.
#   cloud      needs an Anthropic-hosted backend or a claude.ai account
#   installer  manages the reference's own distribution
#   surface    belongs to a product this app does not ship
#   platform   blocked by the OS or runtime available here
#   retired    the reference itself marks it removed
#   portable   nothing blocks it; it is simply not built yet
#   partial    carried, with a named piece of it missing
#   diverged   carried under the reference's name, backed by a different source
#   addition   this app has it and the reference does not
# A "portable" row is a decision to defer, not a decision to decline: it is the
# work list. A "diverged" row is the more dangerous kind — the name matches, so
# nothing looks wrong until someone assumes the behaviour matches too.
# The mcpserver/mcptool kinds cover the desktop shell's own in-process MCP
# servers — the tools the reference proxies to the model as mcp__{server}__{tool}
# from InternalMcpServerManager.createProxyServers. They were invisible to this
# manifest until 2026-09-01: the file could describe a missing CLI tool but had
# no vocabulary for a whole server, so ten of them went unrecorded while the port
# registered their tools under bare names instead.

the PR bar's merge mode, which the reference reaches only from a stacked or related PR row; its own prMode for the current branch never returns it, and this build draws only the branch's own row, so the mode is unreachable here too

the origin gutter icon beside a session row and its header, which names where the session runs (Local, SSH, Cloud, Remote Control). Every session here is local, so the icon would carry one value forever
the reference's own row for a session whose context was cleared in place; /clear here starts a new session rather than clearing the open one, so the row has no occasion to appear

the header menu's Debug submenu (Export, Copy debug info, Debug share, View CCR debug info). The reference gates the whole submenu on the empty string, so its own build never draws it either; this app has the Debug pane instead

the reference opens its own guided skill-creation chat; this app opens a Code session in the project carrying a prompt that invokes the skill-creator skill it ships, which is the same work through the surface this build has
the ccd menu's only subtitle marks a CLI command shadowing a host one; one command list here has no such collision to mark
the "Default" badge can carry this tooltip naming which settings file set the default; the reference's own Code surface calls its builder without that argument, and this build has one source to name
the palette's navigation row for Claude Design, gated on its own "omelette" capability
an Open in row that hands the session to Claude Desktop, a different application
the session menu row that edits a cloud session's environment; a local session has no environment to edit
the five Cowork rows of Help > Troubleshooting (VM debug logging, SDK debugging, Free Up Cowork Disk Space, and the two Delete Cowork VM rows); Cowork is a product this app does not ship
a Help > Troubleshooting row that writes allowDevTools into the reference's developer_settings.json and unlocks its Developer menu; this build has no such gate and no devtools to unlock

Auto now uses a bounded provider-side allow/ask/deny classifier plus explicit permission rules and permission floors. Its local same-provider classifier and default-mode policy are not Anthropic's private classifier service or consent batching; the reference confirmation dialog is not copied as a claim of that service.
a Bypass row that navigates to /settings/claude-code to switch the mode on; this build has no per-account bypass switch to send anyone to

CLI calls now have shared usage and configured list-price metering with nullable unknown cost. The Desktop Usage page still disables its cost chart when persisted turns do not contain usable cost estimates; no account billing tariff or invoice source is supplied.
the composer's fast-mode switch routes the turn through Anthropic's faster-output path for the account; there is no such route on a key this app holds
a card on the reference's home surface naming a feature chosen by a server-side feed; there is no feed here to choose one
the Usage page's "Token limit" card: a cap an organization sets on the account, with the window it resets in. There is no account here to carry one
the Code composer's draft-only Linear import reads the issue through the user's claude.ai Linear connector; the GitHub half of that pair needs only gh and is portable, the Linear half is not
the palette's Ctrl+Shift+I row opens a chat that is not stored against the account; every session here is a file on this machine and there is no account to keep one out of

the tool-group header's "received {n} events" clause. It counts the task-board events the reference threads through a group (its taskEvents/events arrays), which come from a board this build has no source for

the tool row's "Manage settings" link. Its opensProjectSettings flag is set by exactly two claude.ai project tools — add_repo ("Added {slug} to project permissions") and the project-settings writer — neither of which exists off the account, so the row would never have a call to sit on

the whole Developer menu, offered only when the reference's own developer settings allow devtools: it loads claude.ai builds, opens its MCP log and toggles GrowthBook overrides, none of which exist here
the reference paginates a long transcript and offers this row above the first message it loaded; this app materialises the whole session when it opens one, so there is never anything earlier to load

The terminal now opens an interactive configured-model picker with effort arrows and a session-only toggle; model hooks can request confirmation. The catalogue comes from this installation's providers rather than the reference account/model-capability service.

the Directory's default sort reads an install count from the claude.ai catalog; the local offers carry no such count, so the order falls back to installed-first then by name, which is what the reference's own list gives when every count is equal

The session menu’s row of the same name ends its Open in submenu’s Continue in group, whose only destination is a hosted runner: every session here runs on this computer, so the group is empty and its label is never drawn
the session menu's project submenu moves a session into a claude.ai project; there is no project layer here, and its rows read from the account's project list

the dictation menu's microphone picker: System.Speech, which is what dictates here, records from the Windows default input device and has no API to be pointed at another one, so a picker could list the devices (WinMM waveInGetDevCaps) and not honour the choice

the six starter templates are carried with their own cron, title, description and prompt; their hover preview illustrations are not, being six bespoke SVG mocks that illustrate a connector output this app does not produce

the home view's second section. The reference lists the claude.ai projects the account belongs to, with their unread counts and threads; this one lists the folders sessions have run in, which is the local thing a row can open

the send button's tooltip lists what the composer can do and the chord for each, but not this row or "Send and stay here": the reference's Enter steers a running turn and cmd+enter queues instead, where this composer's Enter already queues while a turn runs, so there is no second thing to bind — and Ctrl+Enter is the permission card's Allow once
the home view's third session kind. The reference reads it from a task board's status; this build has no board, so a session lists as blocked or unread and never as review or working

a Help > Troubleshooting row driving Electron's netLog for thirty seconds with the taskbar showing progress; the engine exposes no equivalent capture, and Settings > Debug already records the provider traffic this app makes
the session menu row that hands a cloud runner back; nothing here holds one
the filter popover's reset row, which the reference draws only in its cowork mode; the code mode gets Clear filters instead, which this build has

the description under that Cloud row. The port used to draw the row and answer it with a dialog explaining there was nowhere to hand the session to, which is a row that never works; it is gone with the destination

The comparison view's vote is research data: the reference POSTs it to ClaudeaiContentService/SaveComparisonFeedback under the organization uuid with both arms' conversation uuids, their models, efforts and thinking modes. There is no such account or endpoint here, so the vote walks its phases and counts itself and is sent nowhere. Nothing else in the flow depends on the request.

the Chat artifacts panel's second tab, beside Artifacts and Files; it holds claude.ai's per-conversation scratch documents, which this build has no store for. The artifact tile's own Download all, Copy as image and Print as PDF actions are carried

the palette's second-pass search: the reference queries its conversation API for matches the cached list did not have. This app's sessions are all local and already listed, so no second pass exists to announce
the palette's navigation row for Claude Security, which runs scans through the account

the diagnostic report modal’s send half: a Reference ID row, a Copy reference ID button and a Send to Anthropic button that posts the bundle as a telemetry event. There is no endpoint here to post it to, and the reference itself renders exactly this shape whenever its own showSendUi is false — no reference row, no send button, Export to file alone. What is carried is the rest of the modal: its four titles, the five contents rows, the scrub note, the Preview contents disclosure with the bundle size, and the saved state’s Show in Explorer and Done
the skill and plugin menus offer a share that publishes to the user's claude.ai account; there is no account here to publish to
the palette's chat row publishes the conversation to claude.ai

the filter's checkbox is carried and stored, but a folder here exists only because a session ran in it, so there is no empty folder for it to reveal Renamed upstream from folders to groups in 1.46388.1.0.

the Code shortcut sheet's one account-gated row: the reference shows it only when its desktop bridge exposes setFastMode and the epitaxy_fast_mode_picker flag is on for a model that has a fast mode. This build has no fast mode. 1.44121.2.0's sheet carries 41 rows with every gate on, and this one carries 39

a skill card's link out to its claude.ai page; the offers here are the packs this build ships and the plugins the configured git marketplaces carry, and none of them has such a page
a project row in the Recents sidebar expands on click and reveals a button that opens the project page; the rows here are the folders sessions have run in, and there is no page to open
the Avatar row is carried as initials over one of the reference's tints, with Randomize avatar and Clear avatar; uploading and cropping an image needs the account that stores it

Local sandbox and its dependent "Strict sandbox mode" row; the reference's Windows sandbox is WSL2-based and neither enabled in the installed build nor configured on this machine, which the sandbox command row already records

Set by MDM profile: the read-only marker a third-party-inference field carries when a device-management profile set it. There is no managed-settings channel here to set one, so every field the window shows is the user's own
the "+" menu's "Add from {github}" attaches a GitHub repository to the conversation as a claude.ai sync source; there is no such store here, so the row is left out rather than rendered dead

the page context menu's spelling half — the dictionary suggestions and Add to dictionary — which WebView2 does not expose (its context-menu target reports no misspelled word, and it has no add-to-dictionary call); the composer carries both against WPF's own checker instead

Real File/form payloads are encoded through the Electron named-pipe bridge into the owning draft, including file-bearing elicit-submit. Trusted activation and frame identity are verified. Configured connector IDs open their connection flow; unknown Claude account catalog IDs need the excluded account directory.

the two artifact kinds of the tool-group header (its hE). The reference reads them off an Artifact call's `action` against two published sets; this build's `artifact` tool renders into an engine tile and takes no action argument, so nothing can resolve to either kind. ToolGroupSummary carries the wording and the oE membership; only the classifier has nothing to feed it
an accent pill inside the Auto row, activated by ArrowRight, opening the reference's auto-mode setup flow; there is no such flow here

disables the picker's Bypass row and names why — an Anthropic account, an internal build, an organization's managed settings, or the CLI session meta's root flag; none of those exists here, so bypass is always offered

Disabled by your organization: the tooltip the reference hangs on a switch an organization policy has turned off, on the Dynamic workflows and Remote Control rows. There is no managed-policy channel here to turn one off, so every switch these pages draw is the user's own

Instructions for Claude is carried, but its description is not: the reference's sentence promises the instructions apply "across chats and Cowork" on every associated account, which is true because the account stores them and the server injects them (its request field include_conversation_preferences). This build stores them locally, so it says so

the frame strips behind the empty chat screen's mascot. Its mechanism, its seven states and its measured constants (waiting 16x600ms, thinking 9x90, writing 8x90, entrance/exit 6x70, tickle 7x40, idle static) are ported into Services/SparkStates.cs and Controls/SparkGlyph.cs, including the steps(frameCount, jump-none) stepping, the one-shot fill:forwards hold and the static fallback for reduced motion and for a sprite that has not loaded. The frames themselves are Anthropic's artwork of the Claude mark, which a rebranded build must not ship, so this steps the active theme's own mark through the same schedule
the proactivity menu sets a server-side stance on Anthropic's models; there is nothing local for the chord to cycle

A panel's model picker also picks that arm's effort and thinking mode, which is why the reference's panel label reads "{model} {effort}". This app's Chat surface has no effort control at all — the reference's own effort chip is the Extended thinking toggle there — so a panel picks a model and the label is the model's name alone.
a menu row kind for a connector's tools, from the chat surface's menu; the ccd builder pushes none

the reference's content-scan verdict (its warning and danger badges) is what puts a skill or plugin in Needs attention; that scan runs on Anthropic's side, so this build uses the local signal it has — a skill or plugin the user switched off

the remaining seven standalone predicates of lQ, which file a call into a run of its own: they name claude.ai project, connector, artifact, cowork and remote-session tools, and the two flags (coordinatorStandalone, sideSessionStandalone) that switch two of them on. Only the MCP-app one has a counterpart here, and it is carried

Saving a vote can also copy a transcript report to the clipboard, with a share link per arm created through /api/organizations/{org}/chat_conversations/{id} — and its two notices for when a link could not be made. Both halves are claude.ai's.

the on-screen indicator a driven desktop wears is carried (Views/ComputerUseGlowWindow.cs) with the reference's own geometry and timings, but drawn natively rather than in a transparent Electron window loading its generated cu-glow.html: the rim says a machine is being driven, and hanging it off the browser engine would leave a fresh install — where that engine has not finished downloading — silently unmarked

How Claude uses the apps you allow (Background / Full control). The Background tier is app-scoped accessibility: its predicate (app.asar YR) requires darwin 15 or later, so isBackgroundModeSupported is false here and the reference renders neither the segmented control nor the two-mode description

Mermaid now renders sanitized selectable inline SVG with width reflow and native ancestor HWND clipping. WPF hosts an Electron child view rather than inserting SVG into the transcript's own DOM; startup without the engine retains the bitmap fallback.
two jarvis:// hosts this build does not route — debug-handoff and preview — which the reference itself answers only in nest builds

a tool row that opens expanded. All three of the reference's sources for it are absent here: el(name) is `name === "PushNotification"` (a cloud tool this port declares), ly is a failed add_repo (a claude.ai project tool), and the question branch needs a tool row for AskUserQuestion, which this app answers with an inline card instead of a row body

the reference layers this key from user settings above a folder's remembered mode and from repo settings below it; this app has one configured default, so the folder layer is consulted only when that default is unset

Indexed Anthropic text/citation deltas now preserve per-claim web links and raw provider citation metadata through streaming, persistence and replay. Document citations retain readable page locators; a local source-document navigation UI and the reference's citation chrome are not reproduced.
Bound-PR Auto-fix and comment controls now drive the real per-session watcher from the CI popover. Their native placement differs from the reference Pull requests section's account-backed control.
the Mobile simulators section's iOS Simulator row; the simulator is macOS-only, as the Claude Code iOS Simulator server row already records

the Computer use section's Accessibility permission row with its Granted / Denied / Not requested / Not supported badge and its "Open System Settings" button; the pane it opens is macOS's Privacy & Security, and Windows reports neither permission
the framebuffer pane, which mirrors a host-published display surface. The reference's own Framebuffer server ends `isEnabled: e => !1`, and there is nothing here to publish a frame source

Separate uses an isolated persistent partition per Code session; new Shared profiles use the measured default workspace partition and ephemeral browsing leaves saved jars intact. Existing Shared accounts keep their original global profile with a visible compatibility explanation. The private flag enabling reference-wide cowork sharing is not remotely synchronized.

Comparison now has attachments, file/image/long-text paste, previews, dictation and the ordinary Chat plus-menu groups. Connector/tool/web-search/project choices apply to both real comparison conversations. This is a native shared-input implementation, not the reference React composer instance; account-only sources keep the ordinary Chat boundary.

the consent footnote links "security guide" here; this app publishes no security guide, and pointing at another product's would present its documentation as ours, so the sentence is carried without the clause

the Scheduled list's source filter (Chat / Code / Slack / Claude, and the switch that reveals routines Claude made itself) sorts rows by which claude.ai surface created them; every routine here is created locally, so the filter would have one value
A footnote under the comparison composer linking an internal Anthropic tool; the reference draws it only for an account carrying that flag.

the persisted half of the allowed-transition store. The reference keeps allowed pairs both in a session map (XM) and in this settings array, and which one a decision lands in is chosen by the card - whose handler registration its shipped build stubs out, so there is nothing to measure about an "always" affordance. This port remembers an allowed pair for the session only, and the pair key it uses is the reference's own "{src}→{dest}"

The reference gives widgets dedicated remote claudemcpcontent.com origins. Jarvis hosts the proxy in Electron and uses sandboxed opaque-origin runtime frames without allow-same-origin; the private remote-origin/account-storage service is not available.

the model selector's "More models" group divides the models the account's catalogue knows from the ids it does not; this build ships no catalogue — every model is one the user added — so the division has nothing to draw
the first-chat onboarding paragraphs are carried; the reference gates them on a server-side rollout variant this client cannot read, so the first chat of all stands in for it

A tool approval that reached only one arm flags that turn's vote, drives a unified approval card across both panels and auto-retries the blocked arm. The Chat surface carries no tools here, so no arm can be blocked on a permission and none of it is reachable.

the hide-before-action pass is carried (Services/ComputerUseHide.cs) with the reference's own never-hide sets, its five-pass frontmost loop and its hidden-apps note, but a window is minimized where the reference's native helper hides it outright: a hidden window can only be restored by the process that hid it, so a crash mid-turn would leave the user's windows gone with nothing on screen to click, where a minimized one is already on the taskbar
the tray menu's plan and usage rows, which read the account's five-hour and seven-day utilisation from claude.ai; the tray here is the reference's Show App and Exit alone

The native media viewer now carries zoom, fit, actual size, panning, previous/next, copy/save and keyboard controls. Its WPF chrome and window placement are native adaptations of the reference CDS component; mixed-DPI secondary-monitor behavior has not been compared.

the pane's domain-transition consent, carried the way the installed build ships it. Still stubbed in desktop 1.46388.2.0, re-measured there: the exported requestDomainTransitionPermission is a function whose whole body is `return "allowed"`, and setPreviewDomainTransitionCardHandler takes its argument and does nothing - so that build never asks, and none of the five sentences its navigate handler (msr) maps the outcomes onto can be reached. BrowserPaneDomainTransitions.RequestAsync mirrors BZt and answers allowed for anything, so this pane asks nothing either. What is missing against the reference is therefore only what the reference itself does not run: the decision behind the stub is DecideAsync, kept beside it and covered, because everything around the stub is live code there too. Measured from it and carried in that machine: the outcome vocabulary, the five sentences verbatim, the $G precondition that both origins are already-allowed pane origins, the U+2192 pair key of launchPreviewAllowedDomainTransitions, the navEpoch staleness re-check, and the 3-per-key / 9-per-session decline caps of the live sibling prompt (zZt's IZt and LZt). What DQt counted as one transition is the single thing its body would have settled and does not: a differing normalized origin (KM, with YM's scheme twin the same site) is inferred from its inputs, its output pair and the module's own normaliser

carried (Services/PreviewOriginPrompt.cs, measured on desktop 1.46388.3.0 where the exported function is real - unlike the domain-transition sibling beside it, which still ships stubbed): the question naming the origin, the line every card carries, the Allow and Cancel buttons with Cancel as both default and escape, the rule that only a tool-driven navigation is gated, and the suppression counts of three refusals for one origin and nine across the session, with an allowed origin clearing its own count. Allowing writes the same list Settings edits, so an origin becomes allowed by being consented to, which is what the domain-transition gate above it is built on. Two pieces are not carried and cannot be: the financial line is selected from a host set read out of a remote feature value that is empty by default, and the higher-risk line from a blocklist category Anthropic serves, so nothing here can classify a site as either - the copy each one selects is kept beside the card rather than invented later. The sentence the model reads on a refusal is this build's own subject over the pane's own declined builder: the reference returns a verdict and words it at a call site that did not resolve in the bundle

the list's "Runs on" filter (cloud / this computer / another computer / local only) sorts rows by the device a routine is bound to; this app schedules nothing off this machine, and the local-only badge it would leave is rendered unconditionally instead
a menu row kind of the chat and Cowork surfaces; the ccd builder pushes none of it, so nothing here can produce one
the cowork://shared-artifact route, which opens an artifact shared through claude.ai; the login and hotkey hosts are likewise account- and macOS-bound and are not routed

the reference tiles one simulator pane per booted device, keyed by udid, and its picker marks a device already shown in another tile "In another tile". This build has one Android Emulator pane per window, so there is one attachment rather than a map, and no second tile for a row to name

The real RichTextBox composer now uses atomic skill nodes with identity/label/hint, selection/removal, loaded undo, rich/plain clipboard and persisted rich drafts. Its editing engine is WPF rather than ProseMirror; measured atom serialization and undo behavior are covered by native control tests.
routes a chosen row to the host or to the CLI; this build has one command list and no CLI bridge to route between
a skill's originating repository, from the claude.ai repo-skills API; the description card renders the line it feeds and nothing here populates it

the unfinished-turn card is carried with its two sentences and both actions; its third state — a lost stream, with "Check now" polling for a reply that may still arrive — needs a conversation this client can re-read from the server, and a local turn has nowhere to poll

the thinking row of the model menu. Its shape is carried - a keepOpen item with a trailing switch that reads out by the mode's title, between the model list and the effort menu - but two of its pieces are not: the mt-1 text-footnote text-muted second line, which renders the mode's own mode_options[].description, and the list of more than one mode its Ag builds from modeOptionsFor(surface)(model). This build lists every session on disk, so that arm is unreachable and is not rendered Re-keyed upstream in 1.46388.1.0; the arm itself is still there.

this app reads the plugins Claude Code has installed (~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json, whose entries name the real install path under cache/{marketplace}/{plugin}/{version}, filtered by that product's own settings.json enabledPlugins). The reference has no counterpart: it IS Claude Code, so its plugin root is its own. Carried for the same reason ~/.claude/skills, .claude/commands, .claude/launch.json and CLAUDE.md are read here - a user whose skills arrive through a marketplace plugin would otherwise see them in one app and not the other, with nothing on screen explaining why. Read-only; this app installs, updates and removes only under its own roots, and its own copy of a name shadows Claude Code's

carried whole (Services/PreviewPorts.cs, the reference's Jor/qor/Gor/Kor at desktop 1.44121.2.0): the tri-state, all seven messages, the fresh-port reassignment and the PORT hand-off its own advice promises. Two adaptations. The messages name the launch file that was actually read rather than the reference's hardcoded .claude/launch.json, because this build resolves .jarvis/launch.json first and advice naming the other one would be an edit that changes nothing - the same swap the closed-pane answer already makes. And the external occupant's process name is read with GetExtendedTcpTable rather than the reference's native listTcpListeners binding; where that cannot answer, the unnamed branch is taken, which is the branch the reference itself takes when its binding is absent

the per-account config blob GET /api/claude_cli/bootstrap returns (401 without a credential), cached as clientDataCacheSlots. It is the reference's second tier for reminder text and its steer, and it can carry prompt text: its zHo reads a map from model pattern to text there. There is no such endpoint here; Settings > General > Reminder text overrides offers a local file in the same shape instead. Measured on CLI 2.1.257: 12 desktop slots across 4 models and 14 days returned one identical payload, and neither tengu_toasty_thimble nor tengu_gentle_parasol was ever served

the GrowthBook remote-eval channel the reference hosts itself: POST {apiHost}/api/eval/{clientKey} with apiHost a hardcoded https://api.anthropic.com/ and clientKey sdk-zAZezfDKGoZuXXKe, evaluated server-side against attributes the client declares. 592 flags on this machine, of which one string carries prose that reaches the model (tengu_hushed_lark_text). No account or flag service exists here, so the local defaults stand

a config-staleness pin the reference reads off the response headers of the Messages call itself, refetching bootstrap mid-session when it differs from the cached client_data's. Gated on tengu_expressive_whistle, false on every account measured, so the reference itself does not act on it; there is no config endpoint here to refetch from either

remote managed settings, which claude doctor reports as "Managed settings (remote)". Its own refusal says it requires an Enterprise or Team subscription; this build has no account tier and reads managed settings only from the machine-wide policy directory

server-delivered startup notices, one of the five prose strings the reference's flag payload carries. Three of those five are UI copy this build has no feed for; the two that reach the model are the reminder text and the Team-onboarding prompt body, both declared with their own rows

the session titlebar's project chip (its Ac -> Ge in caec4a2d4-BpkOzf3_.js): a link to {base}/project/{id} carrying the project's own icon, colour and name. It reads a claude.ai project a local session has no counterpart for

the titlebar origin slot's ssh, bridge and remote kinds. Its pp/mp rule is ported whole in Services/SessionOriginIcon.cs, but this build starts no session over SSH, no bridged session and no cloud one, so only the local arm is reachable and the connection states its mp recolours never occur

the titlebar's popout controls (its Fh: return to the main window, and the always-on-top pin). A session here is a tile in one window's mosaic or a split-view pane; there is no per-session popout window for those two controls to act on
the titlebar's agent badge is drawn and wired (ChatSurface.RunningAsAgent) but nothing sets it: a teammate here runs as a subagent inside a session rather than owning one, so no session is an agent's

the second arm of the origin row's pill slot, which hides on compaction where the folder pill collapses to its icon. Measured on desktop 1.46388.2.0: the caller passes it as the negation of the label it would otherwise show, so the hiding arm is taken only when the pill is one of the two this build has no counterpart for - the repo and location pill of a remote session, and the environment-name pill. Both are cloud, so carrying the arm would add a branch nothing here can reach. It was filed portable until the caller was read

the virtualizer takes a ref to a Set of item indices and unions it into the rendered range, so a listed row stays mounted after it leaves the window. Two of the inputs its Chat transcript computes are carried, measured on desktop 1.46388.2.0: the tail of Zg = 3 rows, and the row that holds focus, which it tracks with a focusin/focusout pair over data-index. Five more are not - a scroll-target index, an array of pinned rows, two boundary indices admitted only below the tail, and a ref array an observer fills - because what each one names was not traced, and a guessed index is a row kept for no reason. The machinery differs and the invariant does not: the reference unions the set into the range it renders, and this generator builds one contiguous run, so a kept row is held from the other end by not being evicted. That cannot create a row nobody scrolled to, which is a difference the reader cannot see - the point of the set is surviving the window, and a row never in it has nothing to survive. This port also holds rows for a live drag selection, which the reference has no counterpart for: a selection whose anchor was evicted is one that cannot be copied

the virtualizer's momentum-scroll compensation: while a touch gesture is in flight the reference folds an anchor correction into a CSS transform rather than writing scrollTop, because inertial scrolling fights a write. WPF's wheel scrolling has no inertia to fight, so this port always takes the branch its own code takes off a gesture and writes the offset

carried as the reference's hasOlder/loadOlder paging with its near-top and unfilled-viewport triggers, but the page comes from the stored session file on disk rather than from a server fetch, so there is no loading state, no retry and no failure to report

the per-session viewport snapshot is the reference's own record and lives for the run as its does, but its keys are server entry uuids where this port derives them from a row's position in the stored session - so a rebuild re-issues every key and the measurements are pruned on each change rather than only when the list shrinks

the five tools get_status, set_monitor, set_auto_merge, bind_pr and unbind_pr, which read the pull request bound to a session and its CI monitor. Measured on desktop 1.46388.3.0: the gate is MD(1776348311), which reads a GrowthBook feature Anthropic serves per account and which defaults to false. The force-on set the build compiles in is empty whenever the app is packaged (CLAUDE_DEV_FORCE_GATES is ignored there), the flag id appears exactly once in the whole bundle - at its own gate - and nowhere in this machine profile, so the installed reference runs none of this. There is a declaration to read and no behaviour to measure a port against, which is why it is filed here rather than as work not yet done. This build reaches the same facts through GitStatusProbe and subscribe_pr_activity, without the server.
